entries.appliesTo: any person offering therapy or psychotherapy services to the public (including via Internet-based AI) and Maine-licensed mental/behavioral health professionals using AI for administrative or supplementary support

dutySources.disclosure-ui: 32 MRSA §2113(3)(A) — 'The client or the client's legally authorized representative is informed in writing of the following: (1) That artificial intelligence will be used; (2) The specific purpose of the artificial intelligence tool or system that will be used'
dutySources.consent-workflow: 32 MRSA §2113(3)(B) — 'The client or the client's legally authorized representative provides consent to the use of artificial intelligence.'
dutySources.human-review: 32 MRSA §2113(4)(C) — 'A licensee may not allow artificial intelligence to: … Generate therapeutic recommendations or treatment plans without review and approval by the licensee.'

exposure.enforcer: unfair-trade-practices (unlicensed AI therapy ban) + licensing-board-discipline (licensee AI-use rules)

sources.aiTherapyRule: 10 MRSA §1500-EE(2) — 'A person may not provide, advertise or otherwise offer therapy or psychotherapy services, including through the use of Internet-based artificial intelligence, to the public unless the therapy or psychotherapy services are provided by a licensed professional.'; 32 MRSA §2113(4)(B) — 'A licensee may not allow artificial intelligence to: … Directly interact with clients in any form of therapeutic communication'
sources.consentRequired: 32 MRSA §2113(3)(B) — 'The client or the client's legally authorized representative provides consent to the use of artificial intelligence.'
sources.scope: 10 MRSA §1500-EE(1)(D) — '"Therapy or psychotherapy services" means services provided to diagnose, treat or address an individual's mental health or behavioral health through therapeutic communication.'
sources.enforcer: 10 MRSA §1500-EE(3) — 'A violation of subsection 2 is a violation of the Maine Unfair Trade Practices Act.'; 32 MRSA §2113(8) — 'A violation of this section is subject to disciplinary action by the board pursuant to Title 10, section 8003, subsection 5.'

flags: Secs. 2-8 enact identical text across seven Title 32 licensing chapters (§§2113, 2600-G, 3300-J, 3820-A, 6207-D, 7009, 13870) covering the mental/behavioral health licensed professions; coded once

Dual enforcement routes with no fine stated in this text: unlicensed-provision ban routed to the Maine Unfair Trade Practices Act (rule 4, no penaltyMax imported); licensee provisions routed to board discipline under Title 10 §8003(5)
Confidentiality duty has no matching duty key: §2113(6) — 'shall ensure that any artificial intelligence technology is compliant with all state and federal confidentiality and privacy laws'

AI use by licensees limited to non-therapeutic 'administrative support' and 'supplementary support'; supplementary support allowed only when 'the client's therapeutic session is recorded or transcribed' (§2113(3)) and AI may not 'Make independent therapeutic decisions' (§2113(4)(A))
Anti-coercion provision: licensee may not deny services because the client 'has not provided consent to the use of artificial intelligence' (§2113(5))
Exception for AI interventions 'used solely within a research project approved by an institutional review board' (§1500-EE(4), §2113(9))
Board rulemaking mandated; rules are 'major substantive rules' (§2113(10)); client waiver void (§2113(11)); private civil actions expressly preserved (§2113(12))
